scope: Vendors and platforms shipping control mechanisms for agents, 2024-06 to 2026-10
notes: 36 items. Primary URLs used where reachable; openai.com, ir.crowdstrike.com and investors.paloaltonetworks.com blocked automated fetches (HTTP 403), so those three items carry primary URLs seen in search results with claims confirmed through contemporaneous coverage (noted per item). Web search budget was exhausted mid-sweep; remaining verification used direct fetches of known announcement pages. Not covered for lack of a dated primary: Docker Sandboxes/MCP Gateway, Cursor sandboxed terminals, OpenAI Codex sandbox, Cisco AI Defense, HashiCorp SPIFFE post (2026-04-30).

items.title: HashiCorp Vault adds native AI agent identities with ceiling policies and per-request authorisation
items.summary: On 12 May 2026 HashiCorp announced native AI agent support in Vault, in early access with a public beta planned. Vault adds an agent registry that tracks agents separately from humans and other non-human identities, and evaluates each agent action as the intersection of the human owner's policies, the agent's baseline policies and ceiling policies that cap its maximum permissions. Per-request authorisation puts permissions in the token itself through an authorization_details claim (OAuth 2.0 Rich Authorization Requests), scoping access to a single task until the token expires.
items.why: Constrain via least-privilege, per-task credentials with an explicit permission ceiling.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date, authors and claims confirmed; the post's GA timeline statements are inconsistent.

items.title: Microsoft Entra Agent ID reaches general availability with agent blueprints, lifecycle governance and Conditional Access templates
items.summary: Microsoft's Entra Agent ID documentation, dated May 2026, states the service is generally available; the exact day is not given, so the first of the month is used here. GA brings agent identity blueprints, an Auth SDK sidecar for token acquisition, integration patterns for non-Microsoft agents on AWS, GCP and n8n, cascade deletion of agent identities, and governance through access packages and sponsor lifecycle workflows that prevent orphaned agents. Conditional Access templates can block high-risk agent identities and set separate policies for autonomous and on-behalf-of agents.
items.why: Agent identity lifecycle and Conditional Access as Constrain and Intervene for enterprise agents.
items.verification_note: Microsoft Learn page fetched; ms.date 2026-05-01, GA stated without a day; month precision.

items.title: Gemini CLI's policy engine applies allow, deny and ask rules to every tool call with admin override
items.summary: Gemini CLI's policy engine evaluates every tool call against TOML rules that return allow, deny or ask_user, with the highest-priority matching rule winning and tiers (default, extension, workspace, user, admin) letting administrator policies override local ones. Rules can target tools, argument patterns, shell command prefixes or regexes, and whole MCP servers, and in non-interactive mode ask_user is treated as deny. The reference page was last updated on 30 April 2026, which is the date used here; the engine's introduction date is not stated, and the docs note the workspace tier was non-functional at the time.
items.why: Constrain via declarative per-tool allow/deny policy with admin override in a coding agent.
items.verification_note: Documentation page fetched; no introduction date given, so the page's last-updated date is used. A third-party explainer dated 2026-03-20 describes the same feature.

items.title: Google Cloud introduces Agent Identity, Agent Gateway and Model Armor integrations at Next 2026
items.summary: At Google Cloud Next in April 2026 Google introduced Agent Identity, Agent Gateway and Model Armor integrations as governance and security controls within its Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Coverage describes Agent Identity as giving each agent its own scoped credentials with delegated human authority, Agent Gateway as applying policy to MCP and A2A traffic between agents and tools, and Model Armor as screening for prompt injection, tool poisoning and data leakage at runtime. The iTWire report is dated 26 April 2026; availability status of each control was not stated.
items.why: Agent identity plus a policy-enforcing gateway: Constrain at the tool boundary.
items.verification_note: iTWire article fetched (2026-04-26); Gateway and Model Armor details from Tamnoon coverage seen in search results (2026-04-24); Google's own announcement post not located in this sweep.

items.title: Anthropic describes Claude Code auto mode, a classifier that reviews each action in place of permission prompts
items.summary: On 25 March 2026 Anthropic described auto mode for Claude Code, which replaces many permission prompts with model-based classifiers that review each proposed action against the user's intent. Anthropic reported that users accept about 93% of manual prompts, which it reads as approval fatigue, and positioned auto mode as lower-maintenance than sandboxing, which is safe but needs reconfiguration whenever a capability requires network or host access.
items.why: Observe and Intervene via a classifier monitor replacing human approval; raises the L2 question of a monitor that is itself a model.
items.verification_note: Primary engineering post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Databricks publishes prompt-injection mitigations for agents built on inherited permissions and deny-by-default egress
items.summary: On 11 March 2026 Databricks published guidance and platform controls for prompt injection in agents, adopting Meta's Rule of Two and the lethal-trifecta framing. It recommends on-behalf-of-user authentication so agents inherit the requesting user's permissions, Unity Catalog privileges and attribute-based controls to limit reachable data, AI Gateway guardrails such as PII detection and Prompt Guard 2 classifiers, deny-by-default serverless egress controls, and monitoring through inference and system tables.
items.why: Manipulation; Constrain (inherited permissions, egress deny-by-default) plus Observe (logging).
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date, authors and claims confirmed.

items.title: Policy for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore becomes generally available in 13 regions
items.summary: On 3 March 2026 AWS made Policy for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore generally available in 13 regions. Policy operates outside agent code and lets administrators centrally restrict what an agent may do without modifying the agent itself. It follows the December 2025 preview that intercepted tool calls at AgentCore Gateway with Cedar policies.
items.why: Constrain enforced by infrastructure rather than by the model.
items.verification_note: AWSInsider post fetched; date and GA claim confirmed; official AWS What's New post for the GA not located.

items.title: Google adds a User Alignment Critic and origin isolation to Gemini agentic browsing in Chrome
items.summary: On 8 December 2025 Google described a layered security architecture for Gemini-powered agentic browsing in Chrome. A User Alignment Critic, a separate Gemini model isolated from untrusted page content, reviews each proposed action and can request a retry or hand control back to the user; Origin Sets restrict the agent to approved sites and elements and block unrelated origins and iframes. Chrome also pauses for manual confirmation before sensitive steps such as banking or Password Manager sign-ins.
items.why: Observe via an isolated trusted monitor plus Constrain (origin scoping) and Intervene (confirmations); a monitor design relevant to the L2 test.
items.verification_note: BleepingComputer article fetched; date and claims confirmed; Google's own post was not reachable in this sweep.

items.title: AWS previews Policy in Bedrock AgentCore to intercept every tool call with Cedar rules
items.summary: On 2 December 2025 AWS previewed Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which works with AgentCore Gateway to check every tool call in real time against defined boundaries. Rules can be written in natural language and are converted into Cedar, AWS's open-source policy language, so enforcement sits outside the agent's code. AgentCore Evaluations, also in preview, adds 13 built-in evaluators plus custom scoring for monitoring agent behaviour in production.
items.why: Constrain via externally enforced per-call policy; Verify and Observe via continuous evaluations.
items.verification_note: AWS What's New post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Auth0 for AI Agents goes GA with Token Vault and CIBA-based asynchronous human approval
items.summary: Auth0 for AI Agents became generally available on 19 November 2025 with four components: User Authentication, Token Vault, Asynchronous Authorization and fine-grained authorisation for RAG. Token Vault stores, manages and refreshes users' OAuth tokens for services such as Google Drive, Jira or Slack so the agent code never holds the credentials. Asynchronous Authorization uses CIBA so an agent can request the user's approval for a critical action and receives a token only after the user approves.
items.why: Constrain (credential brokering) and Intervene (out-of-band human approval before consequential actions).
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Microsoft announces Agent 365 as a control plane with an agent registry, quarantine and policy templates
items.summary: At Ignite on 18 November 2025 Microsoft announced Agent 365, which it calls the control plane for AI agents, available through its Frontier early-access programme. A registry built on Entra inventories agents from Microsoft, open-source and third-party platforms and lets IT quarantine unsanctioned agents; each agent gets a unique agent ID that limits its access, policy templates apply standard security rules, and telemetry, dashboards and alerts cover the fleet. Defender handles threat detection and Purview blocks sensitive-data leaks.
items.why: Deploy-and-assure: inventory, identity, policy and observability composed into one stack.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Google and the Kubernetes community announce Agent Sandbox for gVisor-isolated agent code execution
items.summary: At KubeCon North America on 11 November 2025 Google announced Agent Sandbox, a Kubernetes primitive for agent code execution and computer use built with the Kubernetes community and intended as a CNCF project. It provides kernel-level isolation through gVisor, with Kata Containers also supported, and a Python SDK that creates and tears down isolated environments; on GKE it uses managed gVisor with pre-warmed pools for fast start. The companion Pod Snapshots feature entered limited preview.
items.why: Constrain via hardened sandboxes for untrusted agent-generated code at fleet scale.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Meta publishes the Agents Rule of Two for limiting prompt-injection damage
items.summary: On 31 October 2025 Meta published the Agents Rule of Two, a design rule for limiting prompt-injection damage. It names three properties: processing untrustworthy inputs, access to sensitive systems or private data, and the ability to change state or communicate externally, and holds that an agent should combine no more than two within a session until injection can be reliably detected. When a task needs all three, Meta says the agent should not run autonomously and needs supervision such as human approval or another reliable validation step.
items.why: Manipulation; a Constrain design pattern (capability partitioning) that does not depend on detecting the attack.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks releases Prisma AIRS 2.0 with agent inventory, inline prompt-injection defence and continuous red teaming
items.summary: On 28 October 2025 Palo Alto Networks released Prisma AIRS 2.0, completing the integration of Protect AI. Its AI Agent Security module discovers and inventories all agents in use, including unsanctioned ones, and provides inline defence against prompt injection and tool misuse; an AI Red Teaming module runs continuous automated testing with more than 500 attack types. The company also launched Cortex AgentiX for building security agents with permission management and traceability.
items.why: Observe and Intervene inline on agent traffic plus Verify via continuous red teaming.
items.verification_note: Primary IR URL seen in search results but blocked automated fetch (403); dateline and claims confirmed from the MarketScreener copy of the release and SiliconANGLE (2025-10-28).

items.title: Anthropic adds OS-level sandboxing to Claude Code and reports an 84% drop in permission prompts
items.summary: On 20 October 2025 Anthropic added OS-level sandboxing to Claude Code's bash tool, with filesystem isolation limiting writes to chosen directories and network isolation routing traffic through a proxy outside the sandbox that enforces a domain allow-list and asks the user before new domains. Anthropic reported that sandboxing cut permission prompts by 84% in internal use and open-sourced the runtime, which uses bubblewrap on Linux and seatbelt on macOS. The post argues that constant approval prompts cause approval fatigue that makes development less safe.
items.why: Constrain (sandbox, egress allow-list) replacing per-action Intervene prompts; L2-relevant because the boundary does not rely on model cooperation.
items.verification_note: Primary engineering post fetched; date and claims confirmed; proxy confirmation flow corroborated by Simon Willison (2025-10-20).

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore reaches general availability with Identity, Gateway and Observability services
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore became generally available on 13 October 2025, with VPC, PrivateLink, CloudFormation and tagging support across its services. Runtime offers session isolation and A2A support; Gateway connects agents to MCP servers and APIs with IAM or OAuth authorisation; Identity adds identity-aware authorisation and a secure vault for refresh tokens; Observability provides CloudWatch dashboards and OpenTelemetry output. The platform places credentials, tool access and tracing in managed infrastructure outside the agent's code.
items.why: Constrain (gateway-mediated tool access, scoped identity) and Observe (traces) at the platform layer.
items.verification_note: AWS What's New post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: 1Password launches Secure Agentic Autofill so browser agents log in without seeing credentials
items.summary: On 8 October 2025 1Password announced Secure Agentic Autofill in early access for customers using Browserbase. Browser agents can sign in to web services without credentials entering the model context or Browserbase logs; each credential request triggers a real-time approval prompt in 1Password on the user's device, and organisations configure which credentials agents may use.
items.why: Constrain (credentials withheld from the agent) and Intervene (human approval per credential use).
items.verification_note: Press release fetched; dateline and claims confirmed.

items.title: OpenAI announces AgentKit and a Guardrails library with PII, jailbreak and prompt-injection checks at DevDay
items.summary: At DevDay on 6 October 2025 OpenAI announced AgentKit, which bundles a visual Agent Builder, a Connector Registry for governing data sources, ChatKit, and built-in evaluation and tracing. Alongside it OpenAI published Guardrails, a configurable safety layer whose checks include PII detection, jailbreak detection, prompt-injection detection, moderation, URL filtering and hallucination detection, used as a drop-in wrapper around the OpenAI client. InfoQ notes OpenAI's guidance on least privilege and explicit consent for connectors.
items.why: Observe and Intervene with classifier guardrails plus connector governance in a mainstream agent toolkit.
items.verification_note: InfoQ article fetched (2025-10-10); Guardrails check list confirmed from the OpenAI Guardrails documentation page (openai.github.io/openai-guardrails-python); openai.com announcement blocked automated fetch.

items.title: Okta announces Okta for AI Agents, bringing agent discovery, identities and governance into its identity fabric
items.summary: At Oktane on 25 September 2025 Okta announced Okta for AI Agents, bringing agents into its identity security fabric. Identity Security Posture Management discovers agents and flags risks tied to service accounts, API keys and OAuth tokens; Universal Directory provisions agent identities with owners and risk classifications; access is governed through least-privilege policies, Cross App Access and Okta Privileged Access, with audit trails of agent actions. Okta scheduled phase one for early access in its fiscal Q1 2027 and general availability later in FY27.
items.why: Deploy-and-assure: agent inventory, ownership and governed credentials.
items.verification_note: Press release fetched; dateline and claims confirmed; roadmap dates are Okta's stated plans.

items.title: Google announces the Agent Payments Protocol with signed Intent and Cart mandates
items.summary: On 16 September 2025 Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) with more than 60 partner organisations, as an extension of A2A and MCP for agent-initiated payments. AP2 uses cryptographically signed mandates backed by verifiable credentials: an Intent Mandate records the user's instructions and limits such as price caps, and a Cart Mandate is signed when the user approves exact items and price, after which the payment method is bound to the cart to create a non-repudiable audit trail. The design separates what the user authorised from what the agent chose.
items.why: Constrain (budget and scope bound in signed mandates) and Observe (audit trail) for the within-budget requirement.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Pangea to add AI detection and response and agent control to Falcon
items.summary: At Fal.Con on 16 September 2025 CrowdStrike announced an agreement to acquire Pangea to add AI Detection and Response to the Falcon platform. CrowdStrike said Pangea's capabilities would give visibility and control over AI agents and workflows, block prompt injection and jailbreak attempts, and monitor shadow AI use. At the same event it launched Charlotte AI AgentWorks, a no-code builder for security agents, and Threat AI agents.
items.why: Observe and Intervene at runtime for enterprise agents; inventory of unsanctioned agents.
items.verification_note: Primary IR URL seen in search results but blocked automated fetch (403); dateline from Business Wire listing (20250916); claims confirmed via SDxCentral and Constellation Research coverage (2025-09-17).

items.title: Cloudflare adds a signed-agents classification using Web Bot Auth request signatures
items.summary: On 28 August 2025 Cloudflare introduced signed agents, a new bot classification for user-directed AI agents whose infrastructure signs HTTP requests with Web Bot Auth message signatures that Cloudflare validates. Site owners can allow or block signed agents as a group in security rules, and the agents are listed in the Radar bots and agents directory. Launch participants included ChatGPT agent, Block's Goose, Browserbase and Anchor Browser.
items.why: Agent identity at the network edge; lets third parties constrain which agents may act on their sites.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date from structured data; claims confirmed.

items.title: Anthropic pilots Claude for Chrome and publishes prompt-injection attack success rates before and after mitigations
items.summary: Anthropic began a controlled pilot of Claude for Chrome with 1,000 Max plan users in late August 2025. In adversarial testing of 123 cases across 29 attack scenarios, browser use without safeguards had a 23.6% prompt-injection success rate, which fell to 11.2% with new mitigations in autonomous mode, and a challenge set of browser-specific attacks dropped from 35.7% to 0%. Defences include per-site permissions, confirmation before high-risk actions such as purchases or publishing, blocked categories such as financial services, and classifiers for suspicious instructions.
items.why: Manipulation; Verify (published attack success rates) alongside Constrain and Intervene controls, with an 11.2% residual failure rate.
items.verification_note: Primary post fetched after redirect from anthropic.com; page metadata shows 2025-08-25, contemporaneous coverage dates the launch 2025-08-26.

items.title: Cloudflare releases MCP Server Portals to put identity policy and tool logging in front of MCP servers
items.summary: On 26 August 2025 Cloudflare released MCP Server Portals in open beta for Cloudflare One customers. A portal is a single endpoint in front of many MCP servers; Cloudflare Access enforces identity, MFA and device-posture policies, shows each user only approved servers and tools, and aggregates request logs showing which tools are invoked. Cloudflare framed the problem in terms of confused-deputy attacks on highly privileged agents.
items.why: Constrain (per-user tool allow-lists at a gateway) and Observe (centralised tool-call logs).
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Okta introduces Cross App Access to route agent-to-app access through the identity provider
items.summary: On 23 June 2025 Okta announced Cross App Access, an extension of OAuth that routes agent-to-application access requests through the enterprise identity provider. When an AI tool needs data from an enterprise app, it requests access from Okta, which checks enterprise policy and issues a token the target app validates, giving IT visibility and control without per-user consent prompts. Okta said it was developing the protocol with ISVs and expected availability to select customers in Q3 2025.
items.why: Constrain via centrally policed agent credentials; Observe via identity-provider logs of agent access.
items.verification_note: Press release fetched; dateline and claims confirmed.

items.title: MCP specification revision makes servers OAuth resource servers and requires RFC 8707 resource indicators
items.summary: The 18 June 2025 revision of the Model Context Protocol classified MCP servers as OAuth resource servers with protected resource metadata and required clients to implement RFC 8707 resource indicators so a malicious server cannot obtain tokens meant for another service. It added a security best practices page, elicitation (servers asking users for more information), structured tool output, and removed JSON-RPC batching. The changes tighten the credential boundary between agents and the tool servers they call.
items.why: Constrain via scoped credentials for tool access; addresses confused-deputy token theft.
items.verification_note: Changelog fetched; revision date is in the URL and page.

items.title: Google details layered defences against indirect prompt injection in Gemini
items.summary: On 13 June 2025 Google's GenAI Security Team described the layered defences deployed in Gemini against indirect prompt injection. They include machine-learning classifiers that detect malicious instructions in emails and files, security reminders around prompt content, markdown sanitisation that blocks external image rendering, URL redaction via Safe Browsing, user confirmation before risky actions such as deleting calendar events, and end-user notifications when a defence fires. Google framed the stack as raising the cost of attack rather than eliminating it.
items.why: Manipulation failure source; Observe (classifiers) and Intervene (confirmations) in a deployed assistant with tools.
items.verification_note: Primary post fetched after redirect from security.googleblog.com; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Microsoft announces Entra Agent ID, giving AI agents directory identities and Conditional Access
items.summary: At Build on 19 May 2025 Microsoft announced Entra Agent ID in public preview, extending identity and access management to AI agents. Agents built in Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry are automatically assigned identities in the Entra directory so they can be managed alongside users with Conditional Access, audit trails and lifecycle policies. Microsoft also announced planned integrations with the ServiceNow AI Platform and the Workday Agent System of Record.
items.why: Agent identity as the basis for least privilege, attribution and revocation.
items.verification_note: Security blog fetched; Conditional Access and preview details from the Entra blog summary seen in search results.

items.title: GitHub's Copilot coding agent runs in a sandbox with a network allow-list and human-gated CI
items.summary: GitHub launched the Copilot coding agent on 19 May 2025 for Copilot Enterprise and Pro+ customers. The agent runs in a sandboxed GitHub Actions environment with internet access limited to a customisable allow-list, can push only to branches it created, and remains subject to existing branch protections and rulesets. Workflows on its pull requests do not run until a human approves them, and the developer who requested the pull request cannot approve it.
items.why: Constrain (sandbox, egress allow-list, branch scope) and Intervene (human approval, separation of duties) for coding agents.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: ServiceNow launches AI Control Tower to inventory and govern first- and third-party agents
items.summary: ServiceNow launched AI Control Tower at Knowledge 2025 on 6 May 2025 and said it was generally available. It gives organisations one place to inventory, govern and track ServiceNow and third-party AI agents, models and workflows, and to assign human managers to oversee agents. It bundles governance, risk and compliance tooling covering security and privacy.
items.why: Deploy-and-assure: fleet inventory and accountable human owners for agents.
items.verification_note: Syndicated press release fetched; servicenow.com copy blocked automated fetch. Dateline confirmed.

items.title: OpenAI ships the Agents SDK with guardrails, handoffs and tracing as built-in primitives
items.summary: On 11 March 2025 OpenAI released the Responses API and an open-source Agents SDK that supersedes its experimental Swarm framework. The SDK's primitives are agents, handoffs between agents, guardrails that run safety checks on inputs and outputs, and tracing that lets developers visualise agent runs. Guardrails and tracing are the SDK's built-in points for constraining and observing agent behaviour.
items.why: Constrain and Observe primitives built into a widely used agent framework.
items.verification_note: InfoQ article fetched (published 2025-03-15); openai.com announcement blocked automated fetch. Launch date 2025-03-11 from coverage.

items.title: OpenAI launches Operator with takeover mode, action confirmations and watch mode on sensitive sites
items.summary: OpenAI released Operator as a research preview for US Pro users on 23 January 2025, a browser agent that completes tasks on websites. It hands control to the user for login credentials and payment details (takeover mode), asks for approval before significant actions such as submitting orders or sending email, requires supervision on sensitive sites such as email and financial services, and declines high-stakes tasks such as banking transactions. A dedicated monitor model flags suspicious behaviour.
items.why: Intervene (confirmation gates, takeover) plus Observe (monitor model) for a consumer browsing agent.
items.verification_note: Primary URL seen in search results but blocked automated fetch (403); safety design confirmed from search summary of the OpenAI page and from Small Business Trends (2025-01-27) and HPCwire (2025-01-24) coverage.

items.title: NVIDIA adds content-safety, topic-control and jailbreak-detection NIM microservices to NeMo Guardrails for agents
items.summary: On 16 January 2025 NVIDIA added three NIM microservices to NeMo Guardrails aimed at agentic applications: content safety, topic control and jailbreak detection. The content safety model was trained on more than 35,000 human-annotated samples, and the services are positioned as small, low-latency models that sit around an agent's inputs and outputs. Amdocs, Cerence AI and Lowe's were named as users of NeMo Guardrails.
items.why: Observe and Intervene through input-output classifiers; an L1 control that does not assume an adversarial agent.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Google's Project Mariner browser agent limits itself to the active tab and asks before purchases
items.summary: Google announced Project Mariner on 11 December 2024, a research prototype browser agent built on Gemini 2.0 and released to trusted testers through a Chrome extension. It can only type, scroll or click in the active tab, and it asks the user for final confirmation before sensitive actions such as purchases. Google said it was studying prompt injection so the agent follows user instructions over malicious third-party instructions.
items.why: Constrain (active-tab scope) and Intervene (confirmation gates) designed in before wider release.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Microsoft introduces the Copilot Control System for governing agents at Ignite 2024
items.summary: At Ignite on 19 November 2024 Microsoft introduced the Copilot Control System, a set of IT controls for adopting Copilot and agents. It covers data protection, management controls for governing access and tracking agent status and lifecycle, and measurement and reporting on adoption. The same post announced new agents (SharePoint agents, Interpreter, Employee Self-Service, Facilitator, Project Manager) to which the controls apply.
items.why: Deploy-and-assure governance layer (inventory, lifecycle, access) for enterprise agents.
items.verification_note: Primary blog post fetched; date and claims confirmed.

items.title: Salesforce makes Agentforce generally available with the Einstein Trust Layer and an agent audit trail
items.summary: Salesforce made Agentforce generally available on 29 October 2024 as a platform for building agents that take autonomous actions across business functions. The Einstein Trust Layer adds zero data retention, toxicity detection, secure data retrieval and dynamic grounding, and an audit trail records agent actions and outputs. In Agent Builder, deployers scope each agent through topics, natural-language instructions per topic and a chosen set of actions, which bounds the work the agent is set up to do.
items.why: Constrain via scoped topics and action lists, Observe via audit trail, in a mass-market enterprise agent platform.
items.verification_note: Press release fetched; dateline and claims confirmed from the body.
